claim: Prom1 is expressed in biliary epithelial cells (BECs) under normal conditions in essentially the same manner as CK19 and EpCAM.
source: We examined the expression pattern of the endogenous Prom1 gene product in the normal adult mouse liver, and confirmed that it was expressed in essentially the same manner as CK19 and EpCAM, which are robust and reliable markers of BECs (Figure 1a,b).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescent staining and FACS analysis data presented in Figure 1a,b showing co-expression patterns.

claim: Prom1 has been reported to be an 'oval cell/liver progenitor cell (LPC) marker' in injured liver.
source: Prom1, better known as the surface antigen CD133, has been reported to be an 'oval cell/liver progenitor cell (LPC) marker' in injured liver (Rountree et al., 2007; Dorrell et al., 2011), but it is also expressed in BECs under normal conditions (Suzuki et al., 2008).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies by Rountree et al., 2007 and Dorrell et al., 2011.

claim: The Prom1-CreERT2;R26R-tdTomato mouse system can be used for specific labeling of BECs.
source: Immunostaining images (Figure 1d) and FACS plot (Figure 1e and Figure 1—figure supplement 1) showed that all of the labeled cells were included in the EpCAM+ BEC population, indicating that the Prom1-CreERT2;R26R-tdTomato mouse can be used for specific labeling of BECs.
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining and FACS analysis data showing that all labeled cells are EpCAM+ BECs.

claim: The labeling efficiency at a tamoxifen dose of 10 mg/20 g mouse body weight was approximately 30%.
source: The labeling efficiency at this dose of tamoxifen was approximately 30% (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative FACS analysis data presented in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Prom1-CreERT2 lineage-labeled and non-labeled BECs show no significant difference in proliferative capacity upon liver injury.
source: We also compared the Prom1-CreERT2 lineage-labeled and non-labeled cells in terms of their proliferative characteristics upon liver injury; using a 5-ethynyl-2'-deoxyuridine (EdU) incorporation assay, and found no significant difference between them (Figure 1—figure supplement 2), showing that their proliferative capacities are indistinguishable.
evidence: The claim is supported by EdU incorporation assay data comparing labeled and non-labeled cells.

claim: The BEC lineage labeling rate of around 30% did not change significantly after ductular reaction was induced by chronic injury.
source: In addition, the BEC lineage labeling rate of around 30% did not change significantly, even after ductular reaction was induced by a chronic injury model (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by FACS analysis data comparing labeling rates before and after TAA injury.

claim: No leakiness of labeling occurred in the absence of tamoxifen administration.
source: We also confirmed that no leakiness of labeling occurred in the absence of tamoxifen administration (Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The claim is supported by FACS analysis data from control mice without tamoxifen treatment.

claim: BEC labeling in the Prom1-CreERT2;R26R-tdTomato system occurs in an un-biased manner.
source: These results indicate that the BEC labeling in our system occurs in an un-biased manner, and that the labeled cells faithfully represent the entire BEC population.
evidence: The claim is inferred from multiple experimental results showing uniform distribution and no difference in proliferative capacity.

claim: The intrahepatic biliary epithelial tissue exhibits a complex yet ordered tree-like structure.
source: As shown in Figure 1c, the intrahepatic biliary epithelial tissue exhibits a complex yet ordered tree-like structure, which cannot be readily recognized by conventional histological analyses of thin tissue sections.
evidence: The claim is supported by X-gal staining and 3D imaging data showing the biliary tree structure.

claim: The basic structural unit of the biliary tree consists of one or two duct tubes running alongside the portal vein with many finer branches (ductules) protruding from the duct and wrapping around the PV.
source: One or two duct tubes run alongside the portal vein (PV) (Figure 2b; PV is not shown), and many finer branches, which we call ductules hereafter, protrude from the duct and wrap around the PV (Figure 2c).
evidence: The claim is supported by 3D imaging data showing the structural organization of the biliary tree.

claim: Pre-existing BECs make a major contribution to the TAA-induced biliary remodeling.
source: The results of the BEC lineage tracing in the 3D tissue architecture strongly suggested that pre-existing BECs made a major contribution to the ductular reaction in the TAA injury model, at least within the initial period of 8 weeks.
evidence: The claim is supported by lineage tracing experiments showing tdTomato+ cells in expanded biliary structures.

claim: The ductular reaction is an extension of branching architecture from the pre-existing biliary tissue, not migration of detached BECs or ectopic emergence of BEC-like cells.
source: Remarkably, none of the expanded branches lost their connectivity with the main duct in the peri-portal area (Figure 2g, white arrows). This indicates that the ductular reaction is neither the migration of detached BECs nor ectopic emergence of BEC-like cells at a distant area in the liver parenchyma, but rather an extension of branching architecture from the pre-existing biliary tissue.
evidence: The claim is supported by 3D imaging data showing continuous connectivity between expanded branches and main ducts.

claim: TAA causes localized cell death of hepatocytes specifically around the central vein.
source: TAA is known to induce localized cell death of hepatocytes, specifically around the central vein (CV).
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge about TAA's mechanism of action.

claim: Continuous administration of TAA causes chronic inflammation and bridging fibrosis, and eventually leads to tumor formation, reminiscent of the progression of fibrotic and cirrhotic liver disease in humans.
source: Continuous administration of this drug causes chronic inflammation and bridging fibrosis, and eventually leads to tumor formation, reminiscent of the progression of fibrotic and cirrhotic liver disease in humans (Yeh et al., 2004; De Minicis et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies on TAA-induced liver injury.

claim: Hepatocytes do not convert into BECs (bilPDs) in the TAA injury model.
source: In the TAA model (as in the DDC model), we did not detect the emergence of hepatocyte-derived EpCAM+ cells (Figure 3e). Intriguingly, even hepatocyte-derived Spp1+ cells were not detected, suggesting that hepPDs are not induced under this injury condition.
evidence: The claim is supported by hepatocyte lineage tracing experiments using rAAV2/8-iCre showing no EpCAM+ or Spp1+ cells derived from hepatocytes.

claim: Hepatocyte-derived duct-like cells (hepPDs) emerge in the DDC model but not in the TAA model.
source: We concluded that hepatocyte-derived duct-like cells (hepPDs) do emerge in the DDC model but not in the TAA model, and that they are distinguishable from bilPDs.
evidence: The claim is supported by comparative lineage tracing experiments in DDC and TAA injury models.

claim: Hepatocyte-derived cells (hepPDs) are Spp1+ MIC1-1C3+ but show little or no expression of CK19, EpCAM, or Prom1.
source: These results are consistent with the report by Tarlow et. al. (Tarlow et al., 2014a) showing that Spp1+ MIC1-1C3+ proliferating ductular cells derived from hepatocytes upon DDC injury (which they named hepPDs) are distinct from those derived from pre-existing BECs (which they named bilPDs) with respect to the gene expression profile. Specifically, such hepatocyte-derived cells (hepPDs) show little or no expression of CK19, EpCAM, or Prom1.
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining and FACS analysis data, and is consistent with cited literature.

claim: BECs exhibit widespread heterogeneity in proliferative capacity in situ.
source: This clearly indicates that the BEC population does not proliferate uniformly as a whole upon injury, but rather, BECs exhibit heterogeneity with regard to their proliferative capacity in vivo.
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative single-cell tracing data showing variable colony sizes.

claim: The duct compartment contained no large colonies of more than five cells, while the peripheral ductule compartment did contain large colonies.
source: First, the duct compartment contained no large colonies of more than five cells, while the peripheral ductule compartment did contain large colonies (Figure 4e–g).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative analysis of colony sizes in different compartments.

claim: The distribution of colony size showed a unimodal distribution pattern with long tail.
source: However, the empirical data showed a unimodal distribution pattern with long tail (Figure 4g and i).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative analysis of colony size distribution data.

claim: Large colonies incorporated a relatively large proportion of the total number of proliferated cells despite their seemingly low proportion.
source: Although the proportion of large colonies was seemingly low, these colonies actually incorporated a relatively large proportion of the total number of proliferated cells (Figure 4h).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative analysis showing the contribution of different colony sizes to total cell numbers.

claim: Most Ki67+ BECs localized to the peripheral area of the biliary tree in TAA injured liver, whereas only a few Ki67+ BECs were seen in the duct around the PV area.
source: Most of the Ki67+ BECs localized to the peripheral area of the biliary tree in the TAA injured liver, whereas only a few Ki67+ BECs were seen in the duct around the PV area (Figure 5a and Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by 3D immunostaining data for Ki67 and CK19.

claim: At 2 weeks of TAA administration, Ki67+ BECs were already enriched in the peripheral ductule region and scattered therein, rather than in the ducts.
source: At 2 weeks of TAA administration, Ki67+ BECs were already enriched in the peripheral ductule region, and scattered therein, rather than in the ducts (Figure 5b).
evidence: The claim is supported by 3D immunostaining data at an early time point of injury.

claim: No defined stem cell niche, such as a cluster or aligned arrangement of Ki67+ cells, was observed in the peripheral ductule compartment.
source: In the peripheral ductule compartment, the Ki67+ cells were widely scattered. No further sign of a defined stem cell niche, such as a cluster or aligned arrangement of Ki67+ cells, was observed.
evidence: The claim is based on analysis of Ki67+ cell distribution patterns in 3D images.

claim: BECs can be classified into two states based on their temporal proliferative capacities: an actively and continuously dividing state and a quiescent state.
source: We hypothesized that BECs could be classified into two states based on their temporal proliferative capacities, and if this was the case, then the relationship between these states could be examined.
evidence: The claim is a hypothesis that was tested using dual nucleotide labeling experiments.

claim: The majority of EdU-labeled BECs were also BrdU-positive, indicating that BECs in the proliferative state tend to remain proliferative.
source: We observed many BrdU and EdU double-positive cells in the biliary tissue structure, and these cells constituted the major part of the EdU-labeled BEC population (Figure 6c,d).
evidence: The claim is supported by dual nucleotide labeling experimental data.

claim: The proportion of BECs that were double-positive in the experiment was statistically significantly different from that theoretically predicted on the assumption that BECs proliferate in an unregulated manner.
source: We also compared the proportion of BECs that were double-positive in our experiment with that theoretically predicted on the assumption that BECs proliferate in an unregulated manner (Figure 6b, lower panel), and found that their difference was statistically significant (Figure 6e).
evidence: The claim is supported by statistical comparison between experimental and predicted data.

claim: The proliferation pattern of BECs conforms to a model in which BECs can take two different states and change from one to the other irreversibly.
source: These results suggest that the proliferation pattern of BECs conforms to a model in which BECs can take two different states and change from one to the other irreversibly (Figure 6b, upper panel).
evidence: The claim is inferred from the dual nucleotide labeling experimental results.

claim: BECs first entered the cell cycle in vivo 6 days after the TAA injury was started.
source: To test this hypothesis, we performed additional immunostaining experiments using Ki67 and found that BECs first entered the cell cycle in vivo 6 days after the TAA injury was started (Figure 7c).
evidence: The claim is supported by time-course Ki67 immunostaining data.

claim: Almost no cell death was detected in the CK19+ area during TAA injury.
source: As expected, almost no cell death was detected in the CK19+ area (Figure 7—figure supplement 2), thus supporting our model prediction.
evidence: The claim is supported by in vivo cell death detection assay data.

claim: Upon liver injury, some BECs are activated to change their growth state to the proliferative state, while the others remain quiescent.
source: Taken together, our results strongly suggest that the proliferation dynamics of BECs upon TAA injury conform to the following stochastic model: (i) upon liver injury, some BECs are activated to change their growth state to the proliferative state, while the others remain quiescent;
evidence: The claim is a conclusion from the mathematical modeling and experimental data.

claim: BECs in the proliferative state can stochastically and irreversibly convert back to the quiescent state during the course of injury.
source: (ii) those BECs that are in the proliferative state can stochastically and irreversibly convert back to the quiescent state during the course of injury;
evidence: The claim is a conclusion from the mathematical modeling and experimental data.

claim: The highly proliferative BEC subpopulation is stochastically maintained and produces a large number of progenies, thereby making a major contribution to the expansion and remodeling of biliary epithelial tissue.
source: (iii) the highly proliferative BEC subpopulation is stochastically maintained and produces a large number of progenies, thereby making a major contribution to the expansion and remodeling of biliary epithelial tissue.
evidence: The claim is a conclusion from the mathematical modeling and experimental data.

claim: The expansion of biliary epithelial tissue is dictated by heterogeneous and stochastic behavior of BECs.
source: Intriguingly, the expansion of biliary epithelial tissue is dictated by heterogeneous and stochastic behavior of BECs.
evidence: The claim is a summary conclusion from the study's findings.

claim: A subset of proliferating BECs that is stochastically maintained, rather than a pre-determined and hard-wired progenitor population, exhibits clonogenic growth potential in vivo and plays a central role in the remodeling of biliary epithelial tissue.
source: Thus, a subset of proliferating BECs that is stochastically maintained, rather than a pre-determined and hard-wired progenitor population, exhibits clonogenic growth potential in vivo and plays a central role in the remodeling of biliary epithelial tissue.
evidence: The claim is a summary conclusion from the study's findings.

claim: The ductule compartment, rather than the ducts, makes a key contribution to tissue remodeling.
source: However, it is the ductule compartment, rather than the ducts, that makes a key contribution to tissue remodeling, as exemplified by the fact that the majority of the proliferating BECs reside in the peripheral ductule region (Figures 4g, 5 and Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative analysis of proliferating cell distribution.

claim: The suppression or failure of ductular reaction leads to exacerbated liver injury and severe defects in liver regeneration.
source: Several lines of evidence involving knock-out mice for regulatory signals, such as TWEAK, HGF/c-Met and FGF7, have collectively demonstrated that the suppression or failure of ductular reaction leads to exacerbated liver injury and severe defects in liver regeneration (Ishikawa et al., 2012; Takase et al., 2013; Lu et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies on knockout mice.

claim: The DDC model is a cholestatic liver injury model that primarily targets the biliary epithelial system.
source: This finding may be of pathophysiological relevance, in that the DDC model is a cholestatic liver injury model that primarily targets the biliary epithelial system, whereas the TAA model is a hepatotoxic injury model with less severe cholestatic disease phenotypes.
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge about different injury models.

claim: The TAA model is a hepatotoxic injury model with less severe cholestatic disease phenotypes.
source: This finding may be of pathophysiological relevance, in that the DDC model is a cholestatic liver injury model that primarily targets the biliary epithelial system, whereas the TAA model is a hepatotoxic injury model with less severe cholestatic disease phenotypes.
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge about different injury models.

claim: The stochastic growth model provides a stable, robust and consistent outcome in a macroscopic view.
source: In other words, the stochastic growth mode provides a stable, robust and consistent outcome in a macroscopic view. This macroscopic feature corresponds to the biliary tree architecture in the macroscopic view, as the biliary tree appears to follow a uniform pattern in both the spatial and temporal terms when it is observed at a large scale (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is inferred from the mathematical modeling results and comparison with experimental observations.

claim: The stochastic behavior of BECs plays a fundamental role in establishing a flexible and adaptive tissue remodeling system in the biliary epithelium.
source: In conclusion, the stochastic behavior of BECs plays a fundamental role in establishing a flexible and adaptive tissue remodeling system in the biliary epithelium, which underlies the robust regenerative capacity of the liver upon injury.
evidence: The claim is a summary conclusion from the study's findings.

claim: Labeled hepatocytes were rarely detected in the experimental setting.
source: It should be noted that, in the present experimental setting, virtually all of the labeled cells were contained within the CK19+ cell population and that labeled hepatocytes were rarely detected (Figure 2h).
evidence: The claim is supported by lineage tracing data showing tdTomato+ cells are CK19+.

claim: The cells that are induced and expanded by the ductular reaction do not show stem or progenitor cell-like activity that contributes to new hepatocytes in most mouse liver injury models.
source: This result is consistent with recent reports by many other groups who have used lineage tracing experiments, in that the cells that are induced and expanded by the ductular reaction, or LPCs, do not show stem or progenitor cell-like activity that contributes to new hepatocytes in most, if not all, models of mouse liver injury (Grompe, 2014; Tarlow et al., 2014b; Yanger et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to recent lineage tracing studies.

claim: rAAV2/8 vector targets hepatocytes in the mouse liver in a highly specific and efficient manner.
source: The rAAV2/8 vector is well known to target hepatocytes in the mouse liver in a highly specific and efficient manner, and has been used in many studies to transfer genes into hepatocytes in vivo.
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge about rAAV2/8 vector properties.

claim: rAAV2/8 vector does not transduce BECs in the adult mouse liver.
source: Importantly, it does not transduce BECs in the adult mouse liver (Yanger et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: Almost all hepatocytes were labeled (more than 97%) by rAAV2/8-iCre injection.
source: FACS analysis of liver cells isolated from these mice confirmed that almost all hepatocytes were labeled (more than 97%; Figure 3b), while EpCAM+ BECs were not labeled (less than 0.1%; Figure 3—figure supplement 1b).
evidence: The claim is supported by FACS analysis data.

claim: EpCAM+ BECs were not labeled (less than 0.1%) by rAAV2/8-iCre injection.
source: FACS analysis of liver cells isolated from these mice confirmed that almost all hepatocytes were labeled (more than 97%; Figure 3b), while EpCAM+ BECs were not labeled (less than 0.1%; Figure 3—figure supplement 1b).
evidence: The claim is supported by FACS analysis data.

claim: Hepatocytes can gain a 'biliary' phenotype in terms of Spp1 expression upon DDC injury, but are not fully converted to BECs as defined by EpCAM expression.
source: This indicates that while hepatocytes can indeed gain a 'biliary' phenotype in terms of Spp1 expression, they are still not fully converted to BECs as defined by EpCAM expression.
evidence: The claim is inferred from immunostaining data showing Spp1+ but EpCAM- cells derived from hepatocytes.

claim: Spp1 and MIC1-1C3 mark a different and broader cell population from that defined by the expression of CK19, EpCAM and Prom1.
source: Thus, Spp1 and MIC1-1C3 mark a different and broader cell population from that defined by the expression of CK19, EpCAM and Prom1.
evidence: The claim is inferred from comparing expression patterns of different markers.

claim: The tissue architecture composed of hepPDs was different from that composed of bilPDs: the former did not form any single and contiguous branch structure but rather formed a subsidiary structure, located just around the pre-existing branched structures of bilPDs.
source: The tissue architecture composed of hepPDs was different from that composed of bilPDs: the former did not form any single and contiguous branch structure but rather formed a subsidiary structure, located just around the pre-existing branched structures of bilPDs.
evidence: The claim is supported by 3D imaging analysis of tissue architecture.

claim: The main contributors to the ductular reaction (in terms of gene expression, cell number, and 3D structure) are pre-existing BECs.
source: The results of these fate-tracing and 3D-imaging analyses confirmed that although hepatocytes are capable of being converted into the biliary epithelial state in a context-dependent manner, the main contributors to the ductular reaction (in terms of gene expression, cell number, and 3D structure) are pre-existing BECs.
evidence: The claim is a conclusion from multiple lineage tracing and imaging experiments.

claim: The labeling was introduced at a rate of less than 0.2% of total BECs for single-cell tracing experiments.
source: 3D imaging and FACS analyses showed that the labeling was introduced at a rate of less than 0.2% of total BECs, and that the labeled cells located singly and apart from each other (Figure 4c,d).
evidence: The claim is supported by FACS and 3D imaging data.

claim: The labeling index of 0.2% did not change even after the injury period.
source: Of note, the labeling index of 0.2% did not change even after the injury period, which is consistent with the notion that the labeling was introduced in an unbiased manner (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by FACS analysis data comparing labeling rates before and after injury.

claim: After 6 weeks of injury, there were still many BECs that had rarely divided and that remained as single cells or merely as clusters composed of a few cells.
source: After 6 weeks of injury, there were still many BECs that had rarely divided and that remained as single cells or merely as clusters composed of a few cells.
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative single-cell tracing data.

claim: Some BECs had undergone several rounds of cell division, forming larger colonies composed of dozens of cells after 6 weeks of injury.
source: At the same time, we also observed larger colonies composed of dozens of cells, indicating that some BECs had undergone several rounds of cell division (Figure 4e,f).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative single-cell tracing data.

claim: No large colonies were found that were directly connected to the duct cells adjacent to PV.
source: Notably, we found no large colonies that were directly connected to the duct cells adjacent to PV.
evidence: The claim is supported by analysis of colony locations in 3D images.

claim: It is not likely that some proliferative cells reside in a fixed position in the duct compartment and continuously supply progeny toward the periphery.
source: Thus, it is not likely that some proliferative cells reside in a fixed position in the duct compartment and continuously supply progeny toward the periphery.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that no large colonies were found connected to duct cells.

claim: The colony-initiating, proliferative cells may reside in the peripheral ductule compartment and relocate their position upon parenchymal injury.
source: Rather, the colony-initiating, proliferative cells may reside in the peripheral ductule compartment and relocate their position upon parenchymal injury.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the distribution of large colonies in the peripheral ductule compartment.

claim: Among non-BEC (CK19-) populations, the majority of the EdU+ cells were BrdU-.
source: By contrast, among non-BEC (CK19-) populations, the majority of the EdU+ cells were BrdU-, confirming that the presence of the double-positive cells was not attributable to insufficient washout of the 1st label.
evidence: The claim is supported by dual nucleotide labeling experimental data serving as a control.

claim: The percentage of BrdU and EdU double-positive cells in the EdU-positive BEC population was approximately 80%.
source: In theory, if our speculation represents reality and the experiment worked perfectly, the percentage of the BrdU and EdU double-positive cells in the EdU-positive population should reach 100%. In practice, however, it was approximately 80% (Figure 6d).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative analysis of dual nucleotide labeling data.

claim: The final labeling rate of the 1st labeling (BrdU) was expected to be approximately 78.5% based on the stochastic model with m = 0.175.
source: In our stochastic model, the timing of the cell cycle entry per day was defined as a Bernoulli process. In this scenario, the final labeling rate of the 1st labeling was expected to be approximately 78.5% (if m = 0.175, then 1-(1-m) ^ 8 = 0.78539).
evidence: The claim is derived from mathematical calculation based on the model parameters.

claim: The observed discrepancy between the experimental data and the theoretical value for the proportion of BrdU and EdU double-positive cells was brought about inherently and could be explained by the proliferative behavior of BECs.
source: Thus, the observed discrepancy between the experimental data and the theoretical value for the proportion of the BrdU and EdU double-positive cells was brought about inherently and could be explained by the proliferative behavior of BECs.
evidence: The claim is inferred from comparing experimental data with model predictions.

claim: The model predicted that the initial ratio of the proliferating BEC population to be p=0.465.
source: The model predicts the initial ratio of the proliferating BEC population to be p=0.465, meaning that the majority of BECs do not divide in response to the injury stimulus.
evidence: The claim is derived from the mathematical modeling results.

claim: The majority of BECs do not divide in response to the injury stimulus.
source: The model predicts the initial ratio of the proliferating BEC population to be p=0.465, meaning that the majority of BECs do not divide in response to the injury stimulus.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the model parameter p=0.465.

claim: The duct compartment cells, which constitute the major part of the BEC population under the normal condition, do not or rarely divide upon injury.
source: This is consistent with the notion that the duct compartment cells, which constitute the major part of the BEC population under the normal condition, do not or rarely divide upon injury (Figure 5).
evidence: The claim is supported by Ki67 immunostaining data showing few proliferating cells in ducts.

claim: The dual nucleotide labeling experiment showed that the proliferative state of BECs switched irreversibly to a quiescent state.
source: The dual nucleotide labeling experiment showed that the proliferative state of BECs switched irreversibly to a quiescent state (Figure 6).
evidence: The claim is supported by dual nucleotide labeling experimental data.

claim: The irreversible switching feature has been reported in a previous study of epithelial tissue in vivo.
source: This feature has also been reported in a previous study of epithelial tissue in vivo (Doupé et al., 2010; Driessens et al., 2012), but is not consistent with a report that described the manner of cell division and cell fate decision in an in vitro model (Spencer et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: BECs may gain a type of steady-state phenotype (or, become more matured and differentiated cells) in order to generate and maintain a functional and robust epithelial tubular structure.
source: We assume that BECs may gain a type of steady-state phenotype (or, become more matured and differentiated cells) in order to generate and maintain a functional and robust epithelial tubular structure.
evidence: The claim is a speculative explanation for the observed irreversible state change.

claim: The stochastic growth model first emerged in the 1960s to explain the heterogeneous behavior of transplanted hematopoietic stem cells.
source: The stochastic growth model first emerged in the 1960s, in order to explain the heterogeneous behavior of transplanted hematopoietic stem cells (Siminovitch et al., 1963; Till et al., 1964).
evidence: The claim is based on citations to historical studies.

claim: Many studies have revealed the existence and role of stochastic behaviour in various phenomena in living things.
source: Since then, many studies have revealed the existence and role of stochastic behaviour in various phenomena in living things (Samoilov et al., 2006).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to a review or study on stochastic behavior.

claim: There is substantial cell-to-cell variation in cell cycle lengths and delay between mitogen re-stimulation and CDK activation.
source: Interestingly, this result agrees with the notion proposed by Spencer et al. (Spencer et al., 2013), confirmed by their single-cell experimental system, that there is substantial cell-to-cell variation in cell cycle lengths and delay between mitogen re-stimulation and CDK activation.
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: Cells had heterogeneous inter-mitotic times, ranging from 20 hr to >50 hr.
source: They also reported that cells had heterogeneous inter-mitotic times, ranging from 20 hr to >50 hr.
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: The biliary tree formed numerous arborization and branch ends around the injured area as the injury progressed.
source: First, as the injury progressed, the biliary tree formed numerous arborization and branch ends around the injured area (Figure 2e–h and Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by 3D imaging data showing structural changes over time.

claim: The location of cycling cells appeared to be scattered at the 3D level.
source: In addition, the location of cycling cells appeared to be scattered at the 3D level (Figure 5a).
evidence: The claim is supported by 3D immunostaining data for Ki67.

claim: Frequent remodeling and sporadic proliferation are well suited to the stochastic growth model, which can maintain a spatiotemporally flexible population of proliferating cells.
source: Such frequent remodeling and sporadic proliferation are well suited to the stochastic growth model, which can maintain a spatiotemporally flexible population of proliferating cells.
evidence: The claim is an interpretation connecting experimental observations to the model.

claim: The detailed shape and degree of expansion of the extended biliary tree varied in each small area of interest.
source: In microscopic view, the stochastic system shows a degree of instability because the cell state may fluctuate and the output may be unpredictable. This feature nicely explains the dynamics of biliary remodeling, in that the detailed shape and degree of expansion of the extended biliary tree varied in each small area of interest (Figure 2h).
evidence: The claim is supported by microscopic observations of tissue structure variability.

claim: In the stochastic model, each cell behaves in a flexible manner, but the total percentages of cells that take each cell-fate decision is strictly defined and follows a particular value at the population level.
source: In our stochastic model, each cell behaves in a flexible manner, but the total percentages of cells that take each cell-fate decision is strictly defined and follows a particular value at the population level (Figure 7a).
evidence: The claim describes a property of the mathematical model.

claim: The biliary tree appears to follow a uniform pattern in both the spatial and temporal terms when it is observed at a large scale.
source: This macroscopic feature corresponds to the biliary tree architecture in the macroscopic view, as the biliary tree appears to follow a uniform pattern in both the spatial and temporal terms when it is observed at a large scale (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by whole-organ imaging data.

claim: Studies in other systems, including hematopoietic stem cells and epidermal homeostasis, have revealed similar models and concepts.
source: Studies in other systems, including hematopoietic stem cells and epidermal homeostasis, have revealed similar models and concepts (Siminovitch et al., 1963; Doupé et al., 2010), implying that a common and fundamental mechanism governs stochastic cell behavior.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to studies in other systems.

claim: Knowledge on the mode of tissue growth provided by this study applies to systems beyond the hepatobiliary system.
source: Knowledge on the mode of tissue growth provided by this study applies to systems beyond the hepatobiliary system, and should provide significant insights into tissue dynamics and homeostasis in many other organs.
evidence: The claim is a speculative statement about the broader implications of the findings.
